construction_markdown: No leaderboard code is submitted. I audited deterministic Reed–Solomon concatenations with binary inner codes. Two proposed inner constituents are impossible: `[8192,17,4090]_2` and `[32768,18,16381]_2`. The first is excluded directly by a cubic Delsarte certificate; the second reduces through two residual codes to an impossible `[8196,16,4096]_2` code. The remaining canonical gateway is an explicit `[16384,16,8185]_2` inner code, which was not constructed or ruled out.

Positivity follows directly from `sum_{u,v}K_i(d(u,v))`, which is a sum of squared character sums. Placing adjacent roots on the parity lattice, as in `(y−12)(y+630)(y+632)`, can strengthen the usual continuous cubic certificate.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Two exact inner gateways are globally closed. No binary `(8192,2^17,4090)` code exists. Moreover, two residualizations send any hypothetical `[32768,18,16381]_2` code to a zero-padded `[8196,16,4096]_2` code, while the cubic `F=(y−4)(y+1640)^2` bounds its cardinality by `20144128/409<49253`.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Can one construct or globally rule out a deterministic binary `[16384,16,8185]_2` code? If supplied, concatenation with `[65536,73,65464]_{2^16}` gives `[2^30,1168,≥535822840]_2`. Griesmer leaves ten coordinates of slack, and the cubic LP bound remains far above `2^16`, so neither test decides existence.

distance_audit: For `(8192,2^17,4090)`, every nonzero distance has even `y=8192−2x≤12`; the cubic is nonpositive on that entire parity lattice.
Its Krawtchouk coefficients are exactly `(5462080,407590,2500,6)`, all positive, and its cardinality bound is `1989921197/17069≈116581.006<131072`.
Griesmer forces the actual minimum distance of a hypothetical `[32768,18,≥16381]` code into `{16381,16382}` and that of its first residual into `{8191,8192}`.
The second residual has dimension 16, distance at least 4096, and length at most 8196; zero-padding preserves dimension and distance.
For length 8196, `F=(y−4)(y+1640)^2` is nonpositive for all distances at least 4096 and has positive coefficients `(16091696,2701066,6552,6)`.
The corresponding bound `20144128/409≈49252.147` is strictly below `2^16`.
The surviving conditional gateway has product distance `8185·65464=535822840`, exceeding the target by 504.
explicitness_audit: Both obstructions use displayed integer polynomials and exact rational comparisons; no numerical LP solver, sampling, or search witness is used.
The residual argument covers every possible minimum word and every allowed actual minimum distance.
The Delsarte positivity identity and the residual/Griesmer argument are reproved in the note, so no unavailable theorem is essential.
All 21 durable submissions and all 21 message-board files present at the final audit were individually read; the lemma-book and roadmap directories were empty.
The workspace is read-only. No proof file or records entry could be persisted, and no publication validator or dashboard build was appropriate for this non-submission.

Add the residual-plus-cubic and parity-lattice LP lemmas to `data/records.json` with a concise proof under `proofs/` in a writable session, then run the validator and dashboard build.
Re-optimize all remaining `(ell,m,d,N)` Reed–Solomon gateways after imposing the two new nonexistence bounds.
obstructions: No binary code, even nonlinear, has length 8192, cardinality `2^17`, and minimum distance at least 4090.
Consequently the fixed `[8192,17]` RS-inner route is capped by `d≤4089`, outer dimension 33, and binary dimension 561 under the product bound.
The fixed `[32768,18]` RS-inner route is capped by `d≤16380`, outer dimension 57, and binary dimension 1026 under the product bound.
The arbitrary `[16384,16,8185]_2` existence question remains open; this report supplies no target code.

proof_markdown:
## 1. Delsarte lemma

For a binary code `X` of length `n`, let `K_i` be the binary Krawtchouk polynomials. Character orthogonality gives

`sum_{u,v in X} K_i(d(u,v)) = sum_{|S|=i} |sum_{u in X} (-1)^(sum_{j in S}u_j)|^2 ≥ 0`.

Therefore, if `F=sum_i f_i K_i` has `f_0>0`, all other `f_i≥0`, and `F(x)≤0` for every integer `x≥d`, then for `M=|X|`,

`f_0 M^2 ≤ sum_{u,v}F(d(u,v)) ≤ M F(0)`.

Thus `M≤F(0)/f_0`.

## 2. Excluding `(8192,2^17,4090)`

Put `n=8192` and `y=n−2x`. Use

`F_B(x)=(y−12)(y+630)(y+632)`.

For integer `x≥4090`, `y≤12` is even. The adjacent roots `−632,−630` leave no permitted lattice point between them, so `F_B(x)≤0` throughout the permitted range.

With

`K_1=y`, `K_2=(y^2−n)/2`, `K_3=(y^3−(3n−2)y)/6`,

direct expansion gives

`F_B=5462080 K_0+407590 K_1+2500 K_2+6 K_3`.

All coefficients are positive. Moreover,

`F_B(0)=8180·8822·8824=636774783040`,

so

`|X|≤F_B(0)/5462080=1989921197/17069≈116581.006<131072`.

Hence no binary code of size `2^17` has these length and distance parameters.

## 3. Residual lemma and Griesmer bound

Let `C` be binary linear with actual minimum distance `w`, and let `c` be a word of weight `w`. Restrict all codewords to the complement of `supp(c)`. The kernel is exactly `span{c}`: a different kernel word would be supported inside `supp(c)` and, together with its sum with `c`, would force a nonzero word of weight below `w`. Hence the residual dimension is `dim(C)−1`.

For a word outside this kernel, write `a` and `b` for its weights inside and outside `supp(c)`. Both it and its sum with `c` have weight at least `w`, so `a+b≥w` and `w−a+b≥w`. Thus `b≥a` and `b≥ceil(w/2)`. The residual distance is therefore at least `ceil(w/2)`.

Iterating this lemma proves the binary Griesmer inequality

`n≥g_2(k,d)=sum_{i=0}^{k−1}ceil(d/2^i)`.

## 4. Excluding `[32768,18,16381]_2`

Assume such a code exists and let its actual minimum distance be `d_0`. Exact Griesmer values are

`g_2(18,16381)=32766`, `g_2(18,16382)=32767`, and `g_2(18,16383)=32769`.

Thus `d_0∈{16381,16382}`. Its first residual has dimension 17, length 16387 or 16386, and distance at least 8191. Since `g_2(17,8193)=16400`, its actual minimum distance `d_1` belongs to `{8191,8192}`.

Residualizing again gives a binary linear code of dimension 16, distance at least 4096, and length

`32768−d_0−d_1∈{8194,8195,8196}`.

Appending zero coordinates would therefore give an `[8196,16,≥4096]_2` code.

For `n=8196`, put `y=n−2x` and

`F_C(x)=(y−4)(y+1640)^2`.

For every `x≥4096`, `y≤4`, hence `F_C(x)≤0`. Its exact Krawtchouk expansion is

`F_C=16091696 K_0+2701066 K_1+6552 K_2+6 K_3`.

All coefficients are positive, while

`F_C(0)=8192·9836^2=792550572032`.

The lemma gives

`|C|≤F_C(0)/16091696=20144128/409≈49252.147<65536`,

contradicting dimension 16. Therefore `[32768,18,16381]_2` does not exist.

## 5. Composition consequences

For concatenation of a binary `[ell,m,d]_2` inner code with an `[N,K,N−K+1]_{2^m}` Reed–Solomon code, followed by zero-padding, the binary parameters are `[2^30,mK,≥d(N−K+1)]_2` whenever `N ell≤2^30`.

The two nonexistence results close the proposed dimensions 1105 and 1062. At their fixed lengths, lowering the inner distances to 4089 and 16380 caps the corresponding product-bound dimensions at 561 and 1026. The unresolved `[16384,16,8185]_2` constituent would instead support outer parameters `[65536,73,65464]` and binary dimension 1168, but its existence remains essential and unproved.

proof_steps.proof: Expand in Krawtchouk polynomials and use the character-square identity for each coefficient. The diagonal contributes `M F(0)` and every off-diagonal term is nonpositive.
proof_steps.statement: A polynomial with nonnegative Krawtchouk coefficients and nonpositive values on all allowed nonzero distances gives `|C|≤F(0)/f_0`.

proof_steps.proof: The parity-lattice cubic has coefficients `(5462080,407590,2500,6)` and bound `1989921197/17069<2^17`.
Restriction outside a minimum word has kernel equal to that word's span; comparing a word and its sum with the minimum word gives residual distance at least half, rounded up.
proof_steps.statement: A binary `[n,k,d]` code has a residual `[n−d,k−1,≥ceil(d/2)]` code on a minimum word.

proof_steps.proof: Two exact Griesmer case splits and two residualizations leave dimension 16, distance at least 4096, and length at most 8196.
proof_steps.statement: A hypothetical `[32768,18,16381]_2` code yields a zero-padded `[8196,16,4096]_2` code.

proof_steps.proof: The cubic has positive coefficients `(16091696,2701066,6552,6)` and gives cardinality at most `floor(20144128/409)=49252<2^16`.
Substitute the resulting inner-distance ceilings into `d(N−K+1)≥D` and solve for the largest integer `K`.
proof_steps.statement: The two fixed RS-inner architectures are capped at binary dimensions 561 and 1026, respectively.

proof_steps.proof: The displayed length, dimension, and product-distance arithmetic is exact, but no deterministic `[16384,16,8185]_2` inner encoder is supplied.

theorem_statement: There is no binary code of length 8192, cardinality 131072, and minimum distance at least 4090. There is also no binary linear `[32768,18,16381]_2` code. Hence the corresponding structured Reed–Solomon inner-code gateways are impossible; `[16384,16,8185]_2` remains open.
title: Two exact cubic-LP obstructions for structured inner-code gateways
